newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil firms lose many colleagues in plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Brazil firms lose many colleagues in plane crash.

text.p: A plane crash which claimed the lives of at least 103 people in Brazil's financial capital of Sao Paulo was keenly felt in the city's exchanges with more than a dozen executives from well-known firms among the dead.
"I was shocked by the accident. It was the first time I have seen so many people (from financial circles) dead," said John Carioba from Indusval brokerage house.
The fact that the flight was an early morning shuttle to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil's second financial center, was seen as the key reason for the long list of executives who died in the crash.
"The time of the flight was terrible, it is exactly when everyone in the financial markets is travelling," he added.
The Fokker-100 aircraft slammed into houses in a densely populated area of Sao Paulo on Thursday morning shortly after take-off, killing all 95 aboard and eight more on the ground.
Some 13 more people injured when the plane crashed into stores and homes are still in the hospital.
As news of the crash filtered into the markets, volume on the Sao Paulo stock exchange dropped noticeably.
"This accident stopped the market. There were many people who lost colleagues in the crash and it took away any desire to work," another trader said.
The funereal atmosphere was clearly seen in turnover which was around half its normal level.
Among the Brazilians who died on the plane were Alberto Coimbra Vieira, 51, corporate director of Banco Itau and Luiz Lauro Romero, head of the research at the National Development Bank (BNDES).
At least eight executives at private bank Unibanco were also on the plane, a company spokeswoman said.
The victims also included Barbara Wright, the wife of Roger Wright, a director of Banco Garantia.
At least one American and two Europeans working in Brazil also perished, officials said.
American David Francis Tobolla, 40, had been a financial director with Citibank Brazil for the past one and a half years after moving from Citibank's office in New York, a Citibank spokeswoman said.
A vice president of the Generali do Brasil, Italian Camillo Marina, also died, confirmed a spokesman at the Italian Consulate. Marina had lived in Brazil since 1974.
"He was the only Italian we know of so far on the plane," the spokesman said.

Also on the doomed flight 402 was Louwerinus Hoogerheide, 48, born in the Netherlands but who had lived in Brazil for much of his life. Hoogerheide was the sales director for food products company Parmalat Brasil.
